theory Denotational

Denotational semantics

Stream-of-states model, semantic equivalence (SemEq), algebraic command laws, and depth-indexed program syntax.

Constable et al. §11.6

Constructive denotational semantics of a small imperative language, following Constable et al., *Implementing Mathematics with the Nuprl Proof Development System* (1986), §11.6.

Meaning is a *stream of states*: given an initial state `a` and a time `n`, `s(a)(n)` is the program state after `n` steps. The domain `S` of well-formed streams is those functions that, once terminated, stay terminated (Figure 11.13). Combinators Abort, Skip, Assign, Concat and IF are the extracted objects of the book’s existence theorems.

This theory formalizes the semantic equivalence relation `SemEq` between streams, proves its equivalence properties (reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity), verifies algebraic command identities (left-absorption of Abort, branch reduction, while-step unfolding), and presents depth-indexed program syntax with denotational interpretation.

25 theorems, 26 abstractions, checked by replaying their tactic scripts on the kernel. Hover any piece of syntax for its kind, surface form, and uniform term; open Tactics, Proof, or Analysis to go deeper.

examples/denotational.nuprl

Original source file
-- | Constructive denotational semantics of a small imperative language,
-- following Constable et al., *Implementing Mathematics with the Nuprl Proof
-- Development System* (1986), §11.6.
--
-- Meaning is a *stream of states*: given an initial state `a` and a time
-- `n`, `s(a)(n)` is the program state after `n` steps. The domain `S` of
-- well-formed streams is those functions that, once terminated, stay
-- terminated (Figure 11.13). Combinators Abort, Skip, Assign, Concat and
-- IF are the extracted objects of the book’s existence theorems.
--
-- This theory formalizes the semantic equivalence relation `SemEq` between
-- streams, proves its equivalence properties (reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity),
-- verifies algebraic command identities (left-absorption of Abort, branch reduction,
-- while-step unfolding), and presents depth-indexed program syntax with
-- denotational interpretation.
theory Denotational

comment book "Constable et al. §11.6: denotational semantics as streams of states."

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Semantic domain (Figure 11.13)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Projections, so spread is readable (the book’s `fst` / `1st` / `2nd`).
abs Fst(p) == let <u, v> = p in u
abs Snd(p) == let <u, v> = p in v

-- Running vs. halted. The store is kept in both cases so sequential
-- composition can pass the final store along (the book’s `State* | Done`
-- drops it at termination; the two encodings are otherwise the same).
abs Status == True ⊎ True
abs Store == Atom → Int
abs State == Store × Status

abs Running(st) == <Fst(st), inl Ax>
abs Halted(st) == <Fst(st), inr Ax>

-- Book: `<st> terminated == decide(<st>; u.void; u.int)`.
abs Terminated(st) ==
  decide (Snd(st)) of inl u => Void | inr u => True

-- Time is an integer; streams are only required to be stable for `n ≥ 0`.
abs StreamTy == State → Int → State
abs Stable(f) ==
  ∀a:State. ∀n:Int.
    Terminated(f a n) → Terminated(f a (n + 1))
abs S == {f:StreamTy | Stable(f)}

-- Book: `T == 1`, `F == 0`, `Bool == {x:int | x=T ∨ x=F}`.
abs Tbit == 1
abs Fbit == 0
abs BoolZ == {x:Int | x = 1 ∈ Int ∨ x = 0 ∈ Int}

-- Semantic equivalence of commands: pointwise equality on all initial states and steps.
abs SemEq(s1; s2) ==
  ∀a:State. ∀n:Int. s1 a n = s2 a n ∈ State

soft Fst, Snd, Status, Store, State, Running, Halted, Terminated
soft StreamTy, Stable, S, Tbit, Fbit, BoolZ, SemEq

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Equivalence properties of SemEq
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem semeq_refl :
  ∀s:StreamTy. SemEq(s; s)
proof
  intro s
  intro a
  intro n
  eq
qed

theorem semeq_sym :
  ∀s1:StreamTy. ∀s2:StreamTy.
    SemEq(s1; s2) → SemEq(s2; s1)
proof
  intro s1
  intro s2
  intro h
  intro a
  intro n
  elim 3 with a THENL [
    hyp,
    elim 6 with n THENL [
      hyp,
      elim 7
      elim 2 with a THENL [
        hyp 4,
        elim 8 with n THENL [hyp 5, hyp 9]
      ]
    ]
  ]
qed

theorem semeq_trans :
  ∀s1:StreamTy. ∀s2:StreamTy. ∀s3:StreamTy.
    SemEq(s1; s2) → SemEq(s2; s3) → SemEq(s1; s3)
proof
  intro s1
  intro s2
  intro s3
  intro h12
  intro h23
  intro a
  intro n
  elim 4 with a THENL [
    hyp,
    elim 8 with n THENL [
      hyp,
      elim 5 with a THENL [
        hyp,
        elim 10 with n THENL [
          hyp,
          elim 11
          hyp 9
        ]
      ]
    ]
  ]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Abort (Abort_thm)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Never takes a step; the stream is constantly “still running”.
abs Abort == λa. λn. Running(a)

soft Abort

theorem abort_never :
  ∀a:State. ∀n:Int. ¬Terminated(Abort a n)
proof
  intro a
  intro n
  reduce
  intro p
  elim 3
qed

theorem abort_in_S :
  Abort ∈ S
proof
  intro with Abort THENL [
    auto,
    intro a
    intro n
    intro p
    reduce
    elim 3
  ]
qed

-- Abort_thm of Figure 11.13: a stream that never terminates.
theorem Abort_thm :
  ∃s:S. ∀a:State. ∀n:Int. ¬Terminated(s a n)
proof
  exists Abort THENL [lemma abort_in_S THEN hyp, lemma abort_never THEN hyp]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Skip
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Skip completes immediately: the stream is constantly halted
-- (zero-duration skip, as in the book’s `Mskip`).
abs Skip == λa. λn. Halted(a)

soft Skip

theorem skip_immediate :
  ∀a:State. ∀n:Int. Terminated(Skip a n)
proof
  intro a
  intro n
  reduce
  intro
qed

theorem skip_stable :
  ∀a:State. ∀n:Int. Terminated(Skip a n) → Terminated(Skip a (n + 1))
proof
  intro a
  intro n
  intro p
  reduce
  intro
qed

theorem skip_in_S :
  Skip ∈ S
proof
  intro with Skip THENL [
    auto,
    intro a
    intro n
    intro p
    reduce
    intro
  ]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Assignment
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

abs Update(s; x; v) == λy. atom_eq y x v (s y)
abs Assign(x; v) == λa. λn. <Update(Fst(a); x; v), inr Ax>

soft Update, Assign

theorem update_hits :
  ∀s:(Atom → Int). ∀v:Int. Update(s; "x"; v) "x" = v ∈ Int
proof
  intro s
  intro v
  reduce
  eq
qed

theorem assign_halts :
  ∀a:State. ∀n:Int. Terminated(Assign("x"; 7) a n)
proof
  intro a
  intro n
  reduce
  intro
qed

theorem assign_lookup :
  Fst(Assign("x"; 7) (<λy. 0, inl Ax>) 0) "x" = 7 ∈ Int
proof
  reduce
  eq
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Sequential composition (Concat_thm) and conditional (If_thm)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- If `s1` is still running at time `n`, keep its state; if it has halted,
-- run `s2` from that halted state for the remaining `n` ticks.
abs Concat(s1; s2) ==
  λa. λn.
    decide (Snd(s1 a n)) of
      inl r => s1 a n
    | inr d => s2 (s1 a n) n

abs IF(r; s1; s2) ==
  λa. λn.
    decide (r (Fst(a))) of
      inl u => s1 a n
    | inr v => s2 a n

soft Concat, IF

-- Concatenating abort on the left is abort: the switch never fires.
theorem concat_abort :
  ∀s2:StreamTy. ∀a:State. ∀n:Int.
    Concat(Abort; s2) a n = Abort a n ∈ State
proof
  intro s2
  intro a
  intro n
  reduce
  eq
qed

theorem semeq_concat_abort :
  ∀s:StreamTy. SemEq(Concat(Abort; s); Abort)
proof
  intro s
  intro a
  intro n
  reduce
  eq
qed

-- Skip is already halted, so concatenation switches to `s2` at once.
theorem concat_skip :
  ∀s2:StreamTy. ∀a:State. ∀n:Int.
    Concat(Skip; s2) a n = s2 (Halted(a)) n ∈ State
proof
  intro s2
  intro a
  intro n
  reduce
  eq
qed

-- Branching is pointwise on the initial store.
theorem if_then :
  ∀s1:StreamTy. ∀s2:StreamTy. ∀a:State. ∀n:Int.
    IF((λst. inl Ax); s1; s2) a n = s1 a n ∈ State
proof
  intro s1
  intro s2
  intro a
  intro n
  reduce
  eq
qed

theorem if_else :
  ∀s1:StreamTy. ∀s2:StreamTy. ∀a:State. ∀n:Int.
    IF((λst. inr Ax); s1; s2) a n = s2 a n ∈ State
proof
  intro s1
  intro s2
  intro a
  intro n
  reduce
  eq
qed

theorem semeq_if_true :
  ∀s1:StreamTy. ∀s2:StreamTy.
    SemEq(IF((λst. inl Ax); s1; s2); s1)
proof
  intro s1
  intro s2
  intro a
  intro n
  reduce
  eq
qed

theorem semeq_if_false :
  ∀s1:StreamTy. ∀s2:StreamTy.
    SemEq(IF((λst. inr Ax); s1; s2); s2)
proof
  intro s1
  intro s2
  intro a
  intro n
  reduce
  eq
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- While (Do_thm): unfold as `IF R THEN (body; W) ELSE Skip`
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- One unfolding of a while-stream, given a recursive call `w`.
abs WhileStep(r; body; w) == IF(r; Concat(body; w); Skip)

soft WhileStep

theorem while_false_is_skip :
  ∀body:StreamTy. ∀w:StreamTy. ∀a:State. ∀n:Int.
    WhileStep((λst. inr Ax); body; w) a n = Skip a n ∈ State
proof
  intro body
  intro w
  intro a
  intro n
  reduce
  eq
qed

theorem semeq_while_false :
  ∀body:StreamTy. ∀w:StreamTy.
    SemEq(WhileStep((λst. inr Ax); body; w); Skip)
proof
  intro body
  intro w
  intro a
  intro n
  reduce
  eq
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Program syntax, depth-indexed by `ind` (the book’s `Statement(d)`)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Abort | Skip | Assign id val
abs Atomic == True ⊎ (True ⊎ (Atom × Int))

-- Statement(0) is empty; Statement(n+1) may use subtrees of depth n.
abs Stmt(n) ==
  ind(n; x,T. Void; Void; x,T. Atomic ⊎ (T × T))

abs Program == (n:Int) × Stmt(n)

soft Atomic, Stmt, Program

theorem stmt0_empty :
  Stmt(0) = Void ∈ U{i}
proof
  eq
qed

-- Atomic meaning function (the `Matomic` of Meaning_thm).
abs MAtomic(q) ==
  decide q of
    inl u => Abort
  | inr r =>
      decide r of
        inl v => Skip
      | inr asg => Assign(Fst(asg); Snd(asg))

soft MAtomic

theorem matomic_abort :
  MAtomic(inl Ax) = Abort ∈ StreamTy
proof
  reduce
  auto
qed

theorem matomic_skip :
  MAtomic(inr (inl Ax)) = Skip ∈ StreamTy
proof
  reduce
  auto
qed

-- A complete (depth-1) program: skip. Exemplary execution test.
theorem skip_program_runs :
  Terminated(MAtomic(inr (inl Ax)) (<λy. 0, inl Ax>) 1)
proof
  reduce
  intro
qed
